candidates.headline: Second Battle of Manassas Rages
candidates.description: Confederate and Union forces clashed near Manassas, Virginia, in a battle that ended the next day in a major Confederate victory under Lee.
candidates.notes: Battle spanned Aug 28-30, 1862; Aug 29 was the second day of heaviest fighting.

candidates.headline: Soviet Union Tests First Atomic Bomb
candidates.description: The USSR detonated its first nuclear device, codenamed First Lightning (RDS-1), at the Semipalatinsk Test Site, ending the US nuclear monopoly.

sources.title: First Lightning: The Soviet Union's First Nuclear Test
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of History and Heritage Resources

candidates.notes: Widely and consistently dated to Aug 29, 1949.

candidates.headline: Thurmond Ends Record Senate Filibuster
candidates.description: Senator Strom Thurmond concluded a 24-hour, 18-minute filibuster against the Civil Rights Act of 1957, still the longest single-senator filibuster on record.

sources.title: Strom Thurmond Filibusters the Civil Rights Act of 1957

candidates.notes: Filibuster began Aug 28 evening and concluded Aug 29, 1957.

candidates.headline: Gemini V Splashes Down
candidates.description: NASA's Gemini V capsule returned to Earth after nearly eight days in orbit, then a spaceflight endurance record, crewed by Gordon Cooper and Pete Conrad.

candidates.headline: The Beatles Play Final Ticketed Concert
candidates.description: The Beatles performed their last official paid concert at Candlestick Park in San Francisco, ending their touring career to focus on studio recording.

sources.title: Candlestick Park: The Beatles' Final Show

candidates.notes: Well documented as their last commercial concert appearance.

candidates.headline: Netflix Is Founded
candidates.description: Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph founded Netflix as a DVD-by-mail rental company in Scotts Valley, California, later becoming a streaming pioneer.
candidates.notes: Incorporation date is well cited as Aug 29, 1997.

candidates.headline: Hurricane Katrina Strikes Gulf Coast
candidates.description: Hurricane Katrina made its second, more devastating landfall near the Louisiana-Mississippi border, causing catastrophic flooding in New Orleans.
candidates.notes: Landfall near Buras-Triumph, Louisiana on the morning of Aug 29, 2005.

candidates.headline: Ingrid Bergman Is Born
candidates.description: Swedish actress Ingrid Bergman was born in Stockholm; she went on to win three Academy Awards across a decades-long international film career.

sources.title: Ingrid Bergman Biography
sources.publisher: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

candidates.notes: Notable for sharing her birth and death date, both Aug 29 (1915-1982).

candidates.headline: Charlie Parker Is Born
candidates.description: Jazz saxophonist and composer Charlie "Bird" Parker was born in Kansas City, Kansas, and became a founding figure of bebop.

sources.title: Charlie Parker
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

candidates.headline: Michael Jackson Is Born
candidates.description: Singer, songwriter, and dancer Michael Jackson was born in Gary, Indiana, later becoming one of the best-selling music artists in history.

candidates.headline: Ingrid Bergman Dies on Her Birthday
candidates.description: Actress Ingrid Bergman died in London at age 67, on the same calendar date as her birth 67 years earlier.

sources.title: Ingrid Bergman Biography
sources.publisher: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

candidates.headline: National Chicano Moratorium March
candidates.description: Roughly 20,000 people marched in East Los Angeles against the Vietnam War in the largest Chicano anti-war demonstration; unrest followed.
candidates.notes: Crowd size and some sequence-of-events details vary across secondary sources; recommend single-source caution.

candidates.headline: Retrospective on Apollo Program Published
candidates.description: A widely circulated magazine retrospective about the Apollo program's legacy was published, reflecting on missions from the preceding two years.
candidates.notes: This is the article's publication date, not the date of any actual mission event - flagged for verifier attention.
